---
title: "Mentoring & Service"
---

Mentoring and service concentrate in three areas for me: guiding and training students for research careers, building peer capacity and community, and serving the field.

## Mentoring

- **Mentor**, Donald Hopkins Pre-Doctoral Scholars Program, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, 2025–present
- **Undergraduate Research Mentor**, UMB/DF-HCC U54 Partnership, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Summer 2026

## Peer capacity and community

- **Organizer**, Writing Accountability Groups, Washington University in St. Louis and Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health. Two recurring groups per academic year serving 10–15 graduate students and postdoctoral trainees, 2018–present
- **Community Advisor**, Graduate Commons Program, Harvard University Housing, 2026–present
- **Co-founder**, R-Ladies Honolulu, part of a global network of free, community-led R education, 2024
- **Alumni Volunteer**, Georgetown Alumni Admissions Program, 2025–present

## University service

- **Postdoctoral Representative**, CEPH Accreditation Site Visit, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, 2026
- **Doctoral Student Representative**, CEPH Accreditation Site Visit, Washington University in St. Louis School of Public Health, 2025

## Professional memberships

Society of Behavioral Medicine; National Communication Association; International Communication Association; Association of Internet Researchers; International Network for Social Network Analysis; American Public Health Association

## Public health practice

Before my doctorate, I spent ten years in public service: as a Health Scientist at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Prevention Research Centers Program, 2014–2017), as a Health Research Analyst contracted to CDC (2010–2014), and as an Epidemiologist with the Georgia Department of Community Health (Georgia Violent Death Reporting System, 2007–2010). My research today remains paired with community-facing work, such as a public science café talk on peer-to-peer health messaging.
